construction_class.name: root-confined parallel construction
construction_class.necessary_condition: After a first split into q parallel slabs, every subsequently used tile is confined to one child slab. All used tiles therefore share one local projective direction modulo q, and their total density must be at least one even if their cosets overlap.

method.proof_rule: For each prime q dividing a tile subgroup order, group all pinned tiles by their local projective kernel direction modulo q and sum their exact densities. A root-confined parallel cover requires at least one direction-class sum to be at least one.
method.stopping_rule: After this declaration is committed, run the frozen producer once and the dependency-free source-first checker once. Retain the obstruction only if the checker reproduces every prime key, subgroup order, local direction, exact class sum, and a global maximum strictly below one.

nonclaims: This does not rule out an overlapping or hybrid finite cover.
This does not prove that no finite cover exists.
This does not establish a globally complete prime pool.
The producer and checker are not a Vela Verification or Decision.

preknowledge.disclosure: An exploratory full-pool direction ledger showed that the proposed pure parallel-root construction is under-supplied at every possible first split; the strongest class is q=2, direction [1,1], at density about 0.5806426.
preknowledge.effect: This iteration receives no Claim credit. Its value is exact qualification of the construction-class boundary and the resulting source-harvest obligation.
